To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
climate policy is more popular when combined with other social and economic policies and when it includes renewable energy standards.

(1) climate policy is more popular when it is combined with other social or economic policy, (2) climate policy is especially popular when combined with policies that are popular with people of color, and (3) the most popular climate policies are clean energy standards that include all technologies, not just renewable energy.
climate policy bundles that also include social and economic policies increase climate policy support, particularly among people of color.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to build public support for ambitious climate action.
how the climate movement can expand its base of support.
a central question of the climate policy literature: how can we make climate action more popular?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
linking climate policies to social and economic issues is effective in increasing support for climate action among the general public.
the results show that the inclusion of climate policy with social and economic policies is an effective way to increase support for climate action among people of color and the general US population.
linking climate policy to economic reforms, especially clean energy standards, and to social reforms, especially affordable housing, can increase public support for climate policy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
climate policy can be made more popular by linking it to social and economic issues.
climate policy is most popular in the US when it is linked to economic and social policy reforms.
linking social and economic policies to climate policies increases public support for climate policy, especially among people of color.
The main takeaway from our work is that
climate advocates should consider the broader context of the climate crisis, and the social and economic impacts of climate policy, when developing climate policy proposals and campaigns.
climate policy can be made popular by combining it with other economic and social policies that are popular with the American public.
linking climate policy to social and economic policy can be a powerful tool for building support for climate action among the general public.
